Most weight loss drugs act by one of three means:

  • Raising core temperature (increased metabolic rate)--this is what DNP does, along with caffeine, ephedrine, and some others. DNP does it best, but is not safe enough to be worth trying IMO.

  • Decreasing appetite--amphetamines are the most famous of these, but there are a ton of appetite suppressants currently used for weight loss. This will work but if you don't have the discipline to maintain a proper diet you will gain the weight right back on stopping the drug.

  • Nutrient absorption blockers--Orlistat. Like you said, these make your shit the consistency of olive oil and fuck your macros in addition to having no long-term effect unless one takes the drug indefinitely.

Ultimately, the only weight loss drugs useful for people with self-control are the first category. No pill can help you if you can't eat right (or at least just not too much) but ephedrine, caffeine, etc. can speed up weight loss for a shorter cut. Please don't take DNP.
